title: Merchant LLM procurement: KMS, SLA & cost tradeoffs
topics: Pricing model for hosted vs dedicated
summary: Procurement + security kickoff to align MSA/DPA redlines, confirm KMS preferences, and clarify SLA levels and pricing implications for hosted vs dedicated deployment. Customer pushing for customer-managed keying + strict egress controls; finance wants final unit pricing before approval. Agreed to run a 4-week pilot with defined SLOs and a pricing cap for the pilot period.
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-18 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Luis (Procurement), Priya (InfoSec), Daniel (Legal), Renee (Platform)

00:00 - Speaker 1 (Avery): Hey everyone thanks for joining — appreciate carving time. Quick roll call, then we'll run through the MSA/DPA asks, KMS options, and the pricing tradeoffs for hosted vs dedicated.
00:22 - Speaker 2 (Luis): Hi yeah Luis here from procurement. We're on a month-end gating, so trying to get clarities on any nonstandard clauses and the final price card.
00:31 - Speaker 3 (Priya): Priya from InfoSec. Main flags: customer-controlled key management, SOC2, audit logs, and egress residency. Also curious about encryption in transit at rest and HSM support.
00:45 - Speaker 1 (Avery): Great — on SOC2 we can provide our attestation and our security pack, for KMS we support both Redwood-managed keying and customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integrations with AWS KMS and GCP CMEK.
01:05 - Speaker 4 (Maya): Just to add, the Private mode (VPC deployment) is where BYOK is fully supported; hosted API can do envelope encryption + customer keys for data-at-rest but there are limits around egress when keys are customer-held.
01:28 - Speaker 5 (Daniel): Daniel (Legal). On the MSA/DPA, we want to limit subprocessing and have tighter data deletion SLAs — 30 days max for retention unless we opt in otherwise. Are you okay with that?
01:42 - Speaker 1 (Avery): We usually do 90 days default retention for logs, but for customer data we can support 30 day retention for certain plans and with limited exceptions. I need to flag that shorter retention has operational impact on cache and inference cost.
02:03 - Speaker 3 (Priya): That's the tension though — shorter retention may reduce caching benefits, which increases per-token cost — finance will push back. Any quant on cost delta?
02:15 - Speaker 2 (Maya): Ballpark: removing prefix/KV caching for a customer who does high-concurrency chat can increase token cost by 20-40% depending on session length. We can run a quick reference calc during the pilot.
02:38 - Speaker 5 (Daniel): On indemnity and liability caps — standard one‑year revenue cap okay for now but procurement might want a higher cap if we do a dedicated deployment with SLA.
02:52 - Speaker 1 (Avery): Noted. For Dedicated we can discuss enhanced liability thresholds as part of the reserved capacity contract.
03:06 - Speaker 3 (Priya): KMS detail: does Redwood's BYOK require sending unencrypted artifacts to your control plane? We need to avoid plaintext leaving our VPC.
03:20 - Speaker 2 (Maya): Good question. For Private (VPC) deployments, keys never leave customer infra — we do a customer-controlled HSM integration. For Hosted BYOK we do envelope encryption where the CMK unwrap occurs in our control plane, which some customers flag.
03:44 - Speaker 4 (Renee): Renee (Platform) — if we go private, what is the maintenance window and upgrade cadence? Our SREs prefer monthly minor updates only.
03:56 - Speaker 2 (Maya): Private deployments have configurable maintenance windows; we generally do rolling updates and can agree to monthly minor and quarterly major upgrades for enterprise customers.
04:12 - Speaker 1 (Avery): Let's pivot to pricing: hosted per-token pricing vs dedicated reserved capacity. Luis, what's your procurement horizon? Pilot first? Annual commit later?
04:25 - Speaker 5 (Luis): Pilot yes. Finance needs the pilot to show predictable unit costs. We might be comfortable with a 6–12 month reserved if the numbers work. Can you share a pilot budget cap?
04:38 - Speaker 2 (Maya): Typically pilots are structured with a fixed monthly cap and metering. We can offer a discounted pilot rate for the first 4 weeks with a hard spend cap; if they exceed we'll notify and pause.
04:56 - Speaker 5 (Daniel): On the DPA, any objection to adding data residency clause locking EU data to EU region? We operate across NA and EU and need region locking.
05:07 - Speaker 1 (Avery): Yes we support region pinning for Hosted — EU data can be pinned to eu-central. For Private it's within your VPC region.
05:20 - Speaker 3 (Priya): Also need audit logs for all admin actions for 1 year — can you retain that?
05:30 - Speaker 2 (Maya): Audit log retention is configurable; our enterprise plan supports 12 months, and we can push longer retention as an addon.
05:44 - Speaker 4 (Renee): What about SLAs? We're trying to map latency SLO to user experience — 95th percentile token latency under 200ms is our target. Can you meet that?
06:00 - Speaker 2 (Maya): For hosted small seq lengths we hit ~100ms 95th on x86 instances; on dedicated GPU pools we can optimize to <150ms for longer contexts. The SLO target of 200ms is reasonable; will depend on model and quantization.
06:20 - Speaker 3 (Priya): If SLA breaks happen, what's the credit model? We need a precise credits schedule in the MSA.
06:30 - Speaker 1 (Avery): We propose service credits by percentage of monthly invoice tied to SLO misses — typical tiers e.g., 99.9% uptime minus X gives Y% credit. We can put a cap at a percent of monthly fees; open to negotiation.
06:50 - Speaker 5 (Luis): Procurement will push to link credits to user-impacting latency too, not just availability.
06:58 - Speaker 2 (Maya): We can include latency-based credits for critical routes (e.g., chat), but that requires agreed-on measurement points and instrumentation hooks which we provide via the Console.
07:15 - Speaker 4 (Renee): Onboarding time — how long to get a private deployment provisioned?
07:23 - Speaker 2 (Maya): Typical turn-up is 4–6 weeks for a first private deployment including network review, keys, and test harness. Hosted pilot can start in days.
07:37 - Speaker 3 (Priya): Any third-party subprocessors? We need the list for the DPA.
07:45 - Speaker 1 (Avery): We'll share the subprocessor list. It's mostly cloud infra providers and monitoring vendors.
07:55 - Speaker 5 (Daniel): Liability carve-outs — we may need a data breach clause requiring notification within 48 hours. Is that acceptable?
08:05 - Speaker 1 (Avery): 72 hours is our standard but we can commit to 48 for high-severity incidents in enterprise plans.
08:19 - Speaker 2 (Maya): Quick note: if KMS is customer-managed and keys never leave your HSM, that can affect forensic logging and supportability — support calls might need key unwrap cooperation.
08:35 - Speaker 4 (Renee): Understood. We'll likely lean private for production and hosted for dev.
08:43 - Speaker 5 (Luis): On pricing we need a clear delta between hosted and dedicated — table with cost per 1M tokens at typical concurrency levels.
08:55 - Speaker 2 (Maya): We'll produce a pricing model with examples: low-concurrency chat vs high-concurrency streaming, and show cost impact of KV caching and quantization.
09:10 - Speaker 5 (Daniel): Legal wants MSA redlines by next week — can you circulate a “redlines accepted / blocked” matrix?
09:18 - Speaker 1 (Avery): Yes we'll send a matrix. We'll also attach the security pack and KMS architecture diagram.
09:30 - Speaker 3 (Priya): For pilot success criteria: 1) latency under 200ms P95 for route X, 2) no data residency violations, 3) cost within 10% of projection. If those are met procurement greenlights next steps.
09:55 - Speaker 2 (Maya): We'll instrument synthetic load and produce an eval doc.
10:05 - Speaker 4 (Renee): Backup / restore policies for private — RPO/RTO?
10:12 - Speaker 2 (Maya): RPO 24h, RTO 6h for private by default; can negotiate.
10:25 - Speaker 5 (Luis): Finance wants a pilot invoice model: prepaid cap or pay-as-you-go?
10:33 - Speaker 1 (Avery): We can do prepaid cap with overage alerts and suspend. Preferred for procurement.
10:44 - Speaker 3 (Priya): Quick note: export controls and data classification — we'll need to map which data goes to what tier.
10:52 - Speaker 2 (Maya): We'll help with a data classification worksheet.
11:05 - Speaker 5 (Daniel): Okay recap?
11:09 - Speaker 1 (Avery): Recap: Redwood to send MSA redline matrix, security pack, KMS architecture, pricing table for hosted vs dedicated with pilot cap, and a proposed 4-week pilot scope with success criteria. Customer to confirm preferred KMS mode (likely private), internal stakeholders for finance signoff, and legal to send initial redlines by next Tues.
11:35 - Speaker 5 (Luis): That's right. We aim to sign pilot terms end of month.
11:42 - Speaker 1 (Avery): Great thanks all. We'll follow up via email and share links to the docs.
11:50 - Speaker 3 (Priya): Thanks.
11:52 - Speaker 4 (Renee): Thanks everyone.
11:54 - Speaker 2 (Maya): Bye.
